Colonial border adjustments in 1881 created a political boundary that separated Makonde communities between Portuguese Mozambique and British-influenced territories, promoting dialectal divergence through administrative separation [d7409287s1p0].
Portuguese linguistic and cultural influence among Mozambique's middle and upper classes contributed to different language prestige and possible schooling language policies on the Mozambican side [d19304s6p0].
Large-scale recruitment of immigrant labour from British East Africa to work mines and railways created contact zones that could introduce non-Portuguese linguistic influences into some Makonde-speaking areas [d7409287s1p0].
Military pacification campaigns and the extension of colonial posts disrupted traditional movement and may have increased local isolation of some Makonde groups, reinforcing dialectal divergence [d74678494s11p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: In what ways did colonial administrations (Portuguese and British) and missionary activity influence Makonde social organization and cultural practices?
sub_answers.text:
Portuguese military campaigns and the establishment of colonial posts imposed new authorities and administrative structures on Makonde communities in northern Mozambique [d74678494s11p0].
Chartered companies and later Portuguese colonial administration exercised control over territory and local elites, altering traditional social hierarchies and governance relations [d7409287s1p0].
Portuguese cultural and linguistic influence shaped elite culture in Mozambique and thereby affected social organization and practices among groups interacting with colonial institutions [d19304s6p0].
The recruitment of African soldiers and auxiliaries into colonial forces integrated some local actors into colonial power structures and altered social roles within Makonde societies [d74678494s11p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How did cross-border trade, migration, and intermarriage affect artistic styles such as Makonde carving and mask-making?
sub_answers.text:
Makonde wood sculpture became a prominent and highly developed art form in northern Mozambique, reflecting local artistic traditions concentrated on the Mozambican side [d19304s6p0].
Cross-border movement during conflicts and pacification, including Makonde flight into neighboring German East Africa, created channels for stylistic exchange and diffusion of carving techniques across the border [d74678494s11p0].
Labour migration of workers from British East Africa to Mozambican projects created interpersonal contacts that could transmit artistic motifs and tools between communities [d7409287s1p0].
Economic links mediated by colonial companies and trade networks facilitated the circulation of carved objects and masks, reinforcing stylistic interactions across borders [d7409287s1p0].

sub_answers.text:
RENAMO commenced an insurgency against the FRELIMO government in 1977, sparking the Mozambican Civil War [d735763s0p0].
The civil war was characterised by severe human rights violations on both sides and crippled the Mozambican economy [d735763s0p0].
The Rome General Peace Accords in October 1992 ended FRELIMO's one-party state and introduced multi-party democratic elections, and RENAMO pledged to abandon its armed struggle and operate politically within the new electoral system [d735763s0p0].
Renewed clashes resumed in 2013 and a second peace agreement in August 2019 resulted in the virtual end of the insurgency, although a RENAMO splinter group continued minor guerrilla operations until December 2021 [d735763s0p0].
FRELIMO was initially formed in exile in neighbouring Tanzania and pursued an anti-traditionalist programme that aimed to wrest social and political power from local tribal authorities as part of a socialist restructuring of society [d735763s1p0].
